protocol: Each dataset uses the same unchanged first 70% normal training samples, chronological held-out prediction, deterministic algorithms and train-only normalization. Labels/scenarios are evaluation context only.
limitations: Computed on deliberately synthetic fixtures; does not establish effectiveness on real MySQL workloads. No positive labels in the normal dataset: recall/F1 there are zero by convention.

warnings: Suspected indicators describe observed deviations from the training baseline; they do not establish root cause.
Tolerance floors are explicit demonstration defaults, not calibrated MySQL capacity limits or an SLA.
Operational alerts require both a raw model anomaly and a metric deviation. This may suppress subtle multivariate anomalies; compare raw predictions and metrics as well.
Test labels contain no anomalies: recall/F1 cannot support a detection-quality conclusion; inspect false positives.

mad.aggregation: maximum absolute robust z-score over selected features
mad.zero_mad: train-only epsilon tolerance; no test-statistic fallback

noise_guard.description: alert = raw anomaly AND any absolute metric deviation > max(threshold * max(1.4826*MAD, IQR/1.349), absolute floor, 5% of train median); training statistics only
noise_guard.score_policy: Model decision scores are unchanged raw margins; larger means more normal. Indicator deviation scores are policy-scaled deviations, not robust z-scores.
noise_guard.score_definition: signed deviation / (allowed_deviation / threshold); when allowed_deviation is zero, signed deviation * threshold using one event as the count resolution

zero_tolerance_score.gate: abs(deviation) > 0 remains independent of the reporting score

metadata.label_policy: explicit held-out point labels (-1 anomaly, 1 normal)
metadata.scope: Chronological multivariate analysis of MySQL activity samples from CSV or a read-only collector; held-out predictions only.
